content: Ban/rate-limit triggers for unofficial WhatsApp clients (cross-checked, MEDIUM): community guidance says enforcement risk tracks behavior more than raw volume — key triggers are sending to non-opted-in/new contacts, identical repeated messages, no replies/no human-like delays, high block/report rate, new/inactive numbers, IP-to-region mismatch, fixed-interval (non-jittered) sends. Observed safe ceilings: new numbers 20-50 msgs/day ramping to 100-200/day by day 10-14; under 30 msgs/hour, risk rises above 60/hr; separate budget for cold/new-chat initiation; 8h active sending window; warm-up on known contacts first; personalization and reply-rate (>=30%) matter more than absolute volume; new-account first 10 days are highest risk. Mitigations used by products (WaSphere, Whapi.Cloud, WAHA, wa-hub): per-session sliding-window rate limiter, global throttle, configurable per-session send delays, typing simulation, number warm-up module, per-session regional proxy isolation, activity safety meter/quality-score monitoring, exponential backoff on throttle errors.
